column8: Mon 16 Nov: 3d store; Singapore matches only cash already received, certified by an accountant; the counting clock behind row 42; a parallel, not Taiwan's rule; the December 2032 date agrees with NUMBERS 4.
Mon 16 Nov: twin of row 1 (the minister's 2017 words: certified cash only, no in-kind, counted a year late); the 2026 terms in row 1 govern.
Mon 16 Nov: 3b; strings turn a gift into a grant, so keeping the half outside the contribution lets Laura's figure be unconditional, as 3d already plans; Singapore's test, not Taiwan's.

Mon 16 Nov: 3b with row 3; her cap works before she pays (the excess stays hers, NUMBERS 4), so what she pays needs no refund clause; pairs with the reserve aha that beating a promise buys almost nothing.
Mon 16 Nov: store; the one scheme that declares rather than excludes a board member's own gift; a contrast for rows 16 and 26 only.

Mon 16 Nov: 3e store; a matcher counts a foreign gift in local money on the day it lands, so the currency gap to December 2032 is hers, which IPS l.15 gives to her flexibility; never a hedge; Singapore dollars, not NT$.
Mon 16 Nov: 3a store; matched money must be used within three to four years while her ten payments run ten; a contrast clause at most.
Mon 16 Nov: store only; 2020-21 audit counts on sponsorships passed off as gifts; serves no part.
Mon 16 Nov: 3a store; Singapore stopped matching endowment and reserve funds in 2018 (the scheme's own label; never call Laura's reserve an endowment); the capital share is unclear on the slide.
Mon 16 Nov: 3e store; matches are rationed and prioritised, so a co-sponsor's match is never certain; IPS l.15 already names a co-sponsor falling short.
Mon 16 Nov: store only; scale of Singapore's fund (600m in all to FY2029; Keel arithmetic agrees with FAQ Q13); context for no part.
Mon 16 Nov: store only; the donor count rests partly on a law firm's note; Singapore's 250% deduction is not Taiwan's tax rule.

Mon 16 Nov: 3d; the door test in a funder's own words, secured and deliverable, which owned Treasuries meet from January 2028 (bottom) and before the 2031 meetings (top), dates as NUMBERS 4; groups' gifts in Hong Kong, not a founder's, and Taiwan asks no bank proof (Q48).
Mon 16 Nov: 3d store; the last 20% waits for the last private dollar, the Asian rhyme of Q11c-021; the December 2032 date agrees with NUMBERS 4.
Mon 16 Nov: 3b store; money above the approved figure is never matched, so an excess paid above her stated top would earn no match either; supports keeping the excess, not the cap analogy.

Mon 16 Nov: 3e store; Hong Kong will not match money from the applicant's controllers; it breaks under Taiwan's own rules, where the owner's own share (自籌) is the match (Q48), so a parallel only; the Asian twin in kind of Q18-010.
Mon 16 Nov: twin of row 6 (a matcher counts in local money; Hong Kong adds that the giver bears the exchange cost).
Mon 16 Nov: 3.0 store; Hong Kong's arts match pays programmes, not capital financing or owned venues; evidence for row 44.
Mon 16 Nov: store only; Hong Kong's ratios and budgets (HK$1.7bn 2016-22, Keel arithmetic checks); a pledge earns no match, though it gets a group through the door (row 13).

Mon 16 Nov: 3d; the plainest exhibit of the two clocks: has or will raise gets a group in, actual cash gets it matched; her dates (stated 2031, paid December 2032) agree with NUMBERS 4; groups, not founders.

Mon 16 Nov: 3.0 and 3a; Hong Kong pays the walls but at most two years of start-up help, and only if the project should become self-sustaining; government heritage buildings, not a private residency; pairs with Q67-016.

Mon 16 Nov: 3a; 27 times is Keel arithmetic and checks (1,704/63) but reflects the scheme's two-year design; that running costs close projects is not shown: say 2 of 12 had stopped unless the audit names the cause; the delays are lateness, not overruns.

Mon 16 Nov: 3a; the commissioner's year-three break-even cliff, when start-up help ends, is the gap ten owned payments close; a press interview, and social enterprises sell services where a residency may not.
Mon 16 Nov: store only; Korea's match tapers for larger firms; corporate gifts, no part.

Mon 16 Nov: 3d; Korea screens whether the giver has the finances to keep supporting the group, the question ten owned payments answer; a firm's accounts, a parallel for what Taiwan's funders might ask.
Mon 16 Nov: twin of row 16 (Korea also excludes a founder's or related party's money); same Taiwan disanalogy (Q48: own funds are the match).
Mon 16 Nov: twin of row 18 (Korea's match also refuses asset and facility costs); cite beside row 18 under row 44.
Mon 16 Nov: 3e store; confirm that the 1.4bn won is fund money only before saying about 48% of the fund money requested was granted; one round of one year.
Mon 16 Nov: store caution only; CONFLICTING totals (ARKO against Newsis), so no Korean total is ever quoted; S held at 2.
Mon 16 Nov: 3.0 store; Korean law may subsidise a private museum only after the state approves its plan; may, within the budget, and museums, not residencies.

Mon 16 Nov: 3.0 and 3a; Korea's 2027 running-cost check rests on a press report, so read the decree before use; replace before the building is even priced (no pricing date exists) with before co-sponsors are asked in 2031; public buildings.
Mon 16 Nov: 3.0 store; empty museums are a visitor problem, not a running-money shortfall: say only that the running-cost test followed building that outran use; NABO is from 2014.
Mon 16 Nov: 3d store; Japan counts only costs already paid, proved by bank records; the strictest counting clock behind row 42.

Mon 16 Nov: 3a; a grant paid after the year needs cash first, and Taiwan's grants also pay in step with receipts (Q48), so a payment each January lets the residency take grants that pay late; a new working-capital use of the ten.
Mon 16 Nov: store only; Japan's fixed grant since FY2022; background to row 43.
Mon 16 Nov: 3d store; the 2009 deficit-filling rule, the only gap-filler found, replaced since FY2022 (row 35), so told in the past tense.
Mon 16 Nov: store only; a pass-through that adds tax status, not money; no part.
Mon 16 Nov: store only; a small pledged-support route that issues receipts only for money received; too detailed for any part.
Mon 16 Nov: store only; investment income about 30% of grants (Keel arithmetic, 219,910/721,035, checks); no part.

Mon 16 Nov: 3c and 3d; a public pledge is owed under Art. 41, but never only once public: a notarised gift contract is also irrevocable (Civil Code Art. 658), whose public-interest list ends in etc.; China's law, not Taiwan's (Taiwan's Civil Code unread); pairs with Q7c-035, owed not owned.

Mon 16 Nov: 3d store; China lets a pledger out if her finances worsen markedly; her bottom is owned so needs no such exit, and the two reasons stay exits, no new rule; the prop-cheque case is a press report.

Mon 16 Nov: 3d; dates agree with NUMBERS 4 and CONCEIT 3, but every door test overclaims: Korea's approved plan and past results are not about money, and no scheme ranks Treasuries above a letter (Gaps); say she passes the money part of each door test; Taiwan asks no bank proof (Q48).

Mon 16 Nov: 3d; Taiwan's proportional cut (Q48) is a capped matcher, not a gap-filler working the other way: only Japan's 2009 rule is a gap-filler here, so drop Taiwan from that side; the top-or-bottom claim is Keel reasoning.

Mon 16 Nov: 3.0 and 3a; say Hong Kong and Korea, never Asia or always; Singapore's fund has matched capital items (row 9), so never say the region's arts matches refuse buildings at all; Korea's rule is a press report; no 2027 ownership claim, good.
